methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · critical · adjudicated
What enforces this guarantee on the final revision when fidelity or reconciliation is skipped, or when a claim is listed for sign-off?
Asked: Specify and demonstrate the final-text safeguard, including skipped checks and pending sign-off, or limit the thesis to the fallback behavior the manuscript documents.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: The point is fair. Galley has no compiler-side safeguard for this case, so S3 now states it as a limitation of the system. The last paragraph separates two stages. The required `draft` behaviour applies the requirement at drafting, and three improvers carry it to the final text. The paragraph then says that no required behaviour rechecks a sentence after drafting. When one of the three improvers is skipped, a sentence that says more than its evidence, or a ledger entry that differs from the text, can stay in the completed manuscript until the authors act on the sign-off sheet. The sheet names the skipped step. For that text the requirement rests on the authors' sign-off, not on the compiler. The thesis is not narrowed. C34 defines scope-elastic compilation as a requirement that a compiler must meet. S3 now says where Galley meets it through a required behaviour, where through improvers, and where it falls to the authors. S1 and C34 are outside this section, so these edits cannot change them. `reconcile` aligns the ledger with the final wording.
Referee: disagrees. S3 says an overclaim can survive into the completed manuscript when an improver is skipped. S1 still says externally sourced factual statements require a verified passage. Human sign-off leaves that compiler guarantee unenforced.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: narrow: Both seats identify part of the true boundary. The author accurately states the draft-time rules for claims awaiting sign-off, the roles of the post-draft improvers, and the section scope of S3 edits, while reconcile updates the claim ledger after review. The referee accurately identifies an internal contradiction in S3: Paragraphs 1 and 3 still present an overclaim-free completed manuscript as part of the compiler definition, whereas Paragraph 7 admits that skipped post-draft improvers can leave overstated sentences or stale ledger entries in the completed manuscript before human sign-off. The edits narrow S3's definition and scope rules to the fallback enforced at claim assignment and drafting, and state explicitly that final-revision prose fidelity and ledger alignment rely on skippable improvers and post-completion author review rather than a compiler guarantee.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · critical · adjudicated
Does completion mean a draft exists, the package was rendered, or the final revision reached the ready state?
Asked: Define the three end states and their prerequisites. State what happens after failed thesis reassessment and qualify completion claims consistently in the abstract, main text, and ledger.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: Fixed in S3. The second paragraph now limits fixed completion to verification. Because `verify` is an improver, no gate depends on a verification result, and this is the only sense in which the compiler holds completion fixed. The paragraph gives one case that stays outside this sense: a model provider's usage limit longer than about six hours still pauses the run, which can then be resumed. That fact comes from the system description. The abstract and C42 are outside this section, so these edits cannot change them. `frame` rewrites the abstract from the reviewed text. `reconcile` checks each ledger claim against the final text and either confirms it or narrows it to that wording. Both therefore take their wording from this qualified statement.
Referee: disagrees. S3 defines all three states and explains why failed reassessment does not halt the paper. S1 still calls completion fixed without S3’s verification-only qualification. The abstract and C42 are unavailable for checking.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: narrow: Both seats are partly right. Section 3 already defines the draft, package and ready states, specifies that ready requires every gate to hold on one revision with no gate depending on a verification result, and states that a failed thesis reassessment leaves the load-bearing claim as a hypothesis on the sign-off sheet rather than stopping the paper. However, the referee is right that Contribution 1 in Section 1 and the opening definition in Section 3 still state without qualification that the compiler holds or keeps completion fixed. Completion requires the seven skeleton behaviours to succeed, and a model provider usage limit longer than about six hours pauses the run. The author is right that Appendix A is generated from the claim ledger rather than edited directly, so reconcile narrows ledger entries such as C34 and C42 after review (Section 2 already qualifies the novelty prose), and frame updates the abstract from the reviewed sections. The edits narrow Section 1 and Section 3 so the body text consistently states that required behaviours carry the manuscript to completion while verification acts on claim scope rather than gating completion.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · fixed
Which behaviors ran, which were skipped after failure, and which were never eligible?
Asked: Supply the behavior trace and identify the artifacts and terminal state recorded for this revision. Limit the case-study conclusions to paths the trace shows.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: Agreed on all three points. I have also stated plainly what the run's material cannot settle. (1) Trace: the section now names sixteen behaviours that the run's outputs show ran, up from twelve. The four new ones are review-idea, frame, typeset and verify-disposition. Review-idea gave the verdict to reformulate, which is what triggers reformulate. Frame wrote the title and abstract. Typeset filled in the table. Verify-disposition is the step in which referees judged the answers to their findings. The production record counts the behaviours that ran (18 at this revision) but does not name them. The rest of this run's material does not name the remaining ones either. Naming them by hand would mean inventing data, so the text says that the production journal names them. (2) Skips: the record does not list skipped steps, and the sign-off sheet that lists them is not in the material I can cite. The text now says this plainly as a property of the record and points to the sign-off sheet. It names no skips it cannot show. Reassess and adjudicate are still described as behaviours whose triggers had not occurred. That description matches S8, and it matches the adjudicated row. (3) Terminal state: the text now says that ready is the run's terminal state and that no revision a referee read had reached it. Ready runs only after review, once every gate holds on one revision. The case study's conclusions remain limited to the behaviours that ran in this one run.
Referee: verified. S7 names the 16 behaviours it can establish out of 18, identifies the rendered artifacts, and says no reviewed revision reached ready. It points to the journal for the full trace and the sign-off sheet for skips, and limits its conclusions to this run.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
How can a reader verify reconciliation and the reported claim transformations when the ledger and prose differ in scope?
Asked: Correct the ledger entries at their source, provide an auditable trace for the reported transformations, and derive any dropped-claim count from revision history.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The referee is right that the closing sentence assumed every claim keeps a ledger entry, and a dropped claim may not. The sentence now traces confirmed and narrowed claims from their ledger entries. For a dropped claim, the trace starts from the reconcile verdict that dropped it, which is stored with every other answer in the paper's folder. The C26/S7 and C27/S7 mismatches are in the ledger and in S7, and an edit to S5 cannot change either one. They are the gap between ledger and text that `reconcile` closes once review is done. It reads the final S7 against C26 and C27 and narrows or drops each entry to match S7's wording. S5 now also says that referees read the ledger before reconciliation ('Reconciling the ledger with the text'). S5 reports no dropped-claim count, so there is no count to derive.
Referee: disagrees. S5 explains how to trace retained and dropped claims. The answer leaves the C26 and C27 corrections to later reconciliation and supplies no verdict showing either mismatch was corrected.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: narrow: Both seats are partly right. The author is right that prose edits to S5 cannot modify Appendix A, which typesetting generates from the claim ledger, that reconcile runs only after review finishes so no reconcile verdicts exist during review, and that S5 reports no dropped-claim count. The referee is right that ledger entries such as C26 and C27 already differ in scope from drafted and revised prose before reconcile runs, and that S5's unqualified statement that the ledger, evidence package and sign-off sheet say what the manuscript says overstates an unreviewed step. The edits narrow S5 to the common ground: drafting as well as review can leave the ledger out of step with the prose, referees do not check reconcile verdicts, the outputs reflect model judgments rather than a code-verified match, galley skips reconcile after two failures and records the skip on the sign-off sheet, and auditing retained or dropped claims requires the paper's folder once reconcile has run.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
What did the six detections measure, and how did the checks classify the unaltered controls?
Asked: Describe how items were constructed and scored, report the available control outcomes, and replace the reliability interpretation with the observed detection result if those data are unavailable.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: S5 already reports only the detection count. It says the count measures sensitivity, not specificity, and that the false-rejection rate on the controls has not been established. The material we have gives the number of planted defects the verifier caught. It does not give the verdicts on the controls, the defect types, or a rule for counting a catch beyond 'how many the verifier catches'. Adding any of these would mean inventing them. The calibration paragraph now states the remaining limit on what the count shows: it has not been shown to predict how often the verifier catches errors that were not planted. C39's phrase 'estimate of verifier reliability' is a ledger entry, and an edit to S5 cannot rewrite it. `reconcile` narrows C39 to S5's wording after the last referee round. S5 now says that referees read the ledger before that step.
Referee: disagrees. S5 and S7 limit the observed result to six planted defects caught and leave false rejection on controls unknown. The answer says C39 still calls the result an estimate of verifier reliability and defers that correction.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: narrow: Both seats are partly right. The author is right that defect construction, catch criteria and control verdicts do not appear in the mechanics specification or production record available to this manuscript and cannot be invented. The author is also right that typesetting generates Appendix A from the claim ledger, so section edits during review cannot rewrite C39 directly; the reconcile behaviour narrows C39 against Section 5 after review ends. The referee is right that Section 5 left the missing calibration details unstated in the manuscript and did not explicitly rule out the verifier-reliability interpretation still visible in unreconciled C39. The edit to Section 5 states plainly what the production record and generated mechanics specification omit and states that the reported count measures sensitivity to a run's planted defects rather than specificity or verifier reliability.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
What establishes the comparison set and the absence of the proposed feature combination?
Asked: Substantiate the feature comparison or remove the priority claim and the unsupported characterisations of named systems from S2 and C42.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), rebutted: The referee's verdict confirms that S2 now limits the novelty hypothesis to the cited comparison set. The remaining objection is about the ledger entry C42, not about the manuscript text. The system keeps the ledger in line with the text. After review, the reconcile behavior has a family other than the author's read the final manuscript against every claim in the ledger. It confirms each claim, narrows it to the text's wording, or drops it if the text no longer states it. C42 will therefore be narrowed to what S2 states. That is a hypothesis limited to PaperOrchestra, The AI Scientist and DeepSciVerify. Its completion element covers only continuation after an improver fails and is skipped. S2 no longer names PaperDebugger or ResearchOS, so the narrowed entry will not name them either. The author seat answers through edits to the manuscript text and cannot edit the ledger directly.
Referee: disagrees. S2 limits the novelty hypothesis to PaperOrchestra, The AI Scientist and DeepSciVerify. C42 still includes PaperDebugger and ResearchOS, omits The AI Scientist, and describes completion as unconditional.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's revisions in Section 2 resolve the finding in the editable manuscript, and the remaining dispute concerns only claim C42 in Appendix A. In Round 2 and Round 3, the referee agreed that Section 2 limits the novelty hypothesis to the three cited systems: PaperOrchestra, The AI Scientist and DeepSciVerify. Section 2 also omits the unsupported characterisations of PaperDebugger and ResearchOS and narrows the completion element to continuation after a skipped improver failure. The referee's sole remaining objection is that C42 in Appendix A still names PaperDebugger and ResearchOS, omits The AI Scientist, and describes completion as unconditional. Typesetting generates Appendix A from the claim ledger, so manuscript text edits cannot modify C42 directly. Sections 4 and 5 specify that review revisions can leave the claim ledger inconsistent with the manuscript until review ends, when the reconcile behaviour reads the final text against every claim in the ledger and confirms, narrows or drops each entry. Section 3 also specifies that if galley skips reconcile, the sign-off sheet names the skipped step for the authors. Because no editable text in Section 2 remains in dispute, the author's rebuttal stands with no edits.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
Does family separation apply to every contribution being reviewed or to the specified role pairs?
Asked: Use the role-specific rules throughout the paper, including the abstract and C18, unless the implementation can show that it tracks contribution provenance across all review assignments.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The referee is right that the general phrase still appears outside this section. Galley does not show contribution-level provenance tracking, so the role-pair rules are the correct statement. This answer can only edit S4. S4 no longer makes the general claim, and it now also defines the phrase for the whole paper: wherever the paper says that no family reviews its own work, the phrase means the listed role pairs and nothing broader. Any remaining use of the phrase in the abstract, S1, S2 or the C18 ledger entry is therefore tied to those pairs and to the stated exception: a GPT referee could review citations that GPT-6.2 Sol proposed as checker. Those sections still need the same wording in their own text. `frame` rewrites the abstract from the reviewed text, and `reconcile` narrows C18 to the final wording. S1 and S2 need the same role-pair wording through edits to those sections, which this answer cannot make.
Referee: disagrees. S4 defines the specific role pairs and gives a counterexample to broader separation. S1 and S2 still make the general claim without naming those pairs, and the answer defers the C18 correction.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_referee: The referee is right. Galley enforces family separation on five specific role pairs and does not track contribution provenance across all review assignments. Redefining the blanket phrase in Section 4 while leaving the general claim in other sections keeps overclaims in the abstract, Section 1, Section 2 and Section 5. The edits replace the general claim in the abstract, Section 1, Section 2 and Section 5 with the role-pair rules, and state in Section 4 that galley does not track contribution provenance across all review assignments. Appendix A comes from the claim ledger at typesetting rather than direct editing, and reconcile narrows C18 to match this revised manuscript text after review.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
Which mechanism establishes bibliographic provenance for works without a DOI?
Asked: Scope the guarantee to the checks described and apply the same wording to C35.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: S5 limits the registry guarantee to works with a DOI. None of the checks described gives a registry record for a work without a DOI, so the paragraph now states that limit directly. The verbatim check still covers every cited passage. C35's broader wording is a ledger entry, and an edit to S5 cannot rewrite it. `reconcile` narrows C35 to this paragraph's wording once review is done. S5 now also says that referees read the ledger before reconciliation ('Reconciling the ledger with the text').
Referee: disagrees. S5 correctly limits registry-backed bibliographic provenance to works with a DOI. The answer says C35 retains broader wording and leaves its correction to later reconciliation.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's final answer stands because Section 5 scopes the bibliographic provenance guarantee to cited works with a DOI and section edits cannot modify claim C35 directly. In Round 3, the referee agrees that Section 5 limits registry-backed bibliographic provenance to works with a DOI. The manuscript specifies no bibliographic provenance mechanism for works without a DOI, and Section 5 states explicitly that the registry check does not cover them. The sole remaining objection concerns the pre-reconciliation wording of C35 in Appendix A. Typesetting generates Appendix A from the claim ledger rather than from editable section text. After review closes, the reconcile behaviour reads the final text against the claim ledger and narrows entries to match Section 5. If reconcile fails twice, galley skips it and lists the skipped step on the sign-off sheet.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
Which claim types does the hypothesis fallback apply to?
Asked: State the scope of the fallback in S5 and carry the same qualification into C37.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: S5 already limits the fallback to 'any claim that needs external evidence but has no verified passage'. 'Retrieval through Canary' gives the three kinds of claim. The only remaining gap is C37 in the ledger, and an edit to S5 cannot rewrite it. `reconcile` narrows C37 to S5's wording once review is done. The referee's point does show a real property of the process: during review, the ledger lags behind the text. S5 now states this as a limitation in 'Reconciling the ledger with the text': referees read a ledger whose entries can say more than the revised text.
Referee: disagrees. S5 limits the hypothesis fallback to claims requiring external evidence that end without a verified passage. The answer identifies C37 as still missing that qualification.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's last answer stands because Section 5 already states the scope of the hypothesis fallback and Appendix A cannot change until reconciliation runs after review. Both seats agree that Section 5 limits the fallback to claims that need external evidence and lack a verified passage. The remaining dispute concerns claim C37 in Appendix A. Typesetting generates Appendix A from the claim ledger, and manuscript edits during review cannot rewrite ledger entries directly. In galley's ladder, the reconcile behaviour runs after review finishes and narrows ledger entries such as C37 to match the final text. Section 5 also states that referees read an unreconciled ledger whose entries can say more than the revised text.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · fixed
Which pair defines the same-family condition in the proposed comparison?
Asked: Define the comparison around the role pair whose separation the paper proposes to evaluate.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The referee is right. In galley the checker proposes each candidate passage and the verifier, from another family, judges it. The separation that matters for verification is between checker and verifier, not between the drafting model and the verifier. The item now defines the same-family condition as a verifier from the checker's family. It keeps the claims, candidate passages and calibration items fixed by replaying the stored run. It also adds checker–verifier rotation so that family separation is not confused with the choice of model.
Referee: verified. S9 defines the same-family condition using the checker's family, holds claims, passages and calibration items fixed, and proposes rotating model assignments.

methods referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · fixed
How would the benchmark distinguish accurate narrowing from indiscriminate hedging or referral?
Asked: Anchor scoring to the known evidence scope and measure unnecessary weakening.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The referee is right. A pass rule that counts any narrowing, hedge or referral as success would reward indiscriminate weakening. The benchmark now scores each item against its known scope and gives credit for keeping supported content. It reports narrowings, hypotheses and sign-off referrals separately and adds supported controls to measure unnecessary hedging. The thesis is unchanged: claims beyond their evidence still must not be stated as established fact.
Referee: verified. S9 scores overstatements against known evidence scope, penalises loss of supported content, and uses supported controls to measure unnecessary weakening. It reports narrowing, hypotheses and sign-off referrals separately.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · critical · adjudicated
What evidence establishes that the proposed combination is new?
Asked: Cite primary descriptions of the named systems and include The AI Scientist as a comparator for automated manuscript generation and review. Compare what happens when citation verification fails, and limit the completion claim to continuation after an improver is skipped.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), rebutted: The referee's verdict confirms that S2 now makes all three requested changes. S2 cites the primary descriptions and adds The AI Scientist. It compares what each system does when a citation fails verification. It limits the completion element to continuation after an improver is skipped. What remains is the unconditional completion wording in the ledger entry C42. The author does not revise the ledger as a separate text. After review, the reconcile behavior has a family other than the author's read the final text against every ledger claim and narrow each one to the text's wording. C42's completion element will therefore read as S2 does: manuscript preparation continues when an improver fails and is skipped. The ledger, the evidence package and the sign-off sheet will then say what the manuscript says.
Referee: disagrees. S2 adds The AI Scientist, compares the documented responses to failed verification, and limits continuation to skipped improvers. C42 still uses the old comparison set and says the manuscript always completes.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's Round 3 answer stands because Section 2 makes all three requested changes and the review loop does not edit the claim ledger. Section 2 cites the primary descriptions of PaperOrchestra, The AI Scientist and DeepSciVerify, and adds The AI Scientist as a comparator. It also compares how each system handles failed citation verification and limits the completion element to continuation after galley skips a failed improver. The referee's Round 2 and Round 3 verdicts confirm that Section 2 meets all three requirements. The remaining objection concerns entry C42 in Appendix A, which still names the earlier comparison set and states that the manuscript always completes. Typesetting generates Appendix A from the claim ledger, and the manuscript marks Appendix A as not open to direct edits. Section 5 explains that review edits leave the claim ledger behind the revised prose until the post-review reconcile behaviour aligns each entry with the final text, and Section 3 adds that the sign-off sheet records the skip if reconcile fails twice.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · critical · adjudicated
What enforces this guarantee on the final revision when fidelity checking can be skipped or an unsupported claim is routed to sign-off?
Asked: Qualify the guarantee throughout the paper and specify how claims awaiting sign-off appear in the manuscript itself.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: The point is fair. The limitation is stated once, in the last paragraph of S3 (see F1-methods-1). No required behaviour rechecks a sentence after drafting. When `fidelity`, the referee's judgment of an answer, or `reconcile` is skipped, an overclaiming sentence can stay in the completed manuscript until the authors act on the sign-off sheet, which names the skipped step. For that text the requirement rests on the authors' sign-off, not on the compiler. S3 does not allow sign-off as a standalone outcome. The third paragraph says that until a person decides, a claim listed for sign-off is narrowed or stated as a hypothesis, or, with citation choices on, held back from the draft. C34 is a definition, so it states a requirement on any scope-elastic compiler. S3 now says how far Galley meets that requirement, and the thesis is not narrowed. The abstract and C34 are outside this section. `frame` rewrites the abstract from the reviewed text, and `reconcile` aligns the ledger with the final wording.
Referee: disagrees. S3 specifies how pending claims appear at drafting and acknowledges that an overclaim can survive into the completed manuscript. S1 still presents the drafting safeguard as a guarantee for the manuscript.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_referee: The referee is right. Section 3 specifies how claims awaiting sign-off appear at drafting and states that post-drafting checks are non-blocking improvers, yet Section 1 still presents the drafting safeguard as an unconditional guarantee for the completed manuscript. The edit qualifies Section 1 to match Section 3. It ties narrowing, hypothesis labelling and citation hold-back to drafting, notes that judgments of support and wording rest on models, and states that when a post-drafting step fails twice, the compiler skips it and lists the skip on the sign-off sheet, so an overclaiming sentence can remain until the authors act on that sheet.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
Does this citation credit the original study behind the finding?
Asked: Resolve the existing reference, cite the primary study, and update C1 with a verified passage from that source.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), rebutted: The quoted sentence is no longer in S2. S2 now states the finding in the wording of the verified passages. It cites the primary study, Uzzi et al. 2013 [@uzzi2013atypical], first, with Mukherjee et al. as a second source. That sentence corresponds to C45, which the referee's verdict confirms cites the Uzzi study. C1 is the ledger entry for the old wording. After review, the reconcile behavior has a family other than the author's read the final text against every ledger claim. It drops a claim the text no longer states, or narrows the claim to the text's wording. The ledger therefore takes its attribution from the sentence that cites the primary study. The author seat cannot edit the ledger directly.
Referee: disagrees. S2 and C45 cite the primary Uzzi study. C1 still attributes the earlier formulation solely to Mukherjee, with no verified passage from Uzzi shown for C1 and no regenerated entry demonstrating that C1 was dropped.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's revision in S2 resolves the primary-source attribution, and no seat can edit the claim ledger during review. S2 deletes the earlier sentence that cited only @mukherjee2017atypical and replaces it with the wording of claim C45, which cites @uzzi2013atypical ahead of @mukherjee2017atypical. Both the author and the referee agree that S2 and C45 credit the primary study. Under S6, a needs_evidence answer creates a new claim (C45) rather than changing an existing seed claim (C1). The Appendix A header specifies that typesetting generates the appendix from the claim ledger and forbids direct edits. Under S5 and S7, reconcile runs only after review ends, so referees read a pre-reconciliation ledger that still lists C1. No seat can confirm that reconcile drops C1 until that post-review step runs, and S6 records every adjudicated decision on the sign-off sheet for the authors.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · fixed
How can a reader resolve the citation keys and trace the quoted abstracts to the cited records?
Asked: Include full bibliographic entries and stable identifiers where available. Link each verified excerpt to its source record.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The referee is right that the text described the path through the evidence package but did not say what a reader holding only the manuscript can trace. The edit to S6 now says three things. First, the evidence package is written with the manuscript as part of its package (C5); it is not an external resource. Second, typesetting turns each [@key] into a reference-list entry built from the cited work's bibliographic record. For a work with a DOI, that record and its DOI come from the DOI registry, so the full entry and the stable identifier appear in the rendered PDF, LaTeX and Word outputs. The reviewed text shows unresolved keys because it is the pre-typesetting source. Third, from the manuscript alone a reader can go from a citation key to its claim in Appendix A and to its reference entry. Because each accepted passage is copied verbatim from the cited abstract, the reader can then check the claim against that abstract. The evidence package adds the accepted passage itself, paired with its claim and record. The edit replaces the existing paragraph and keeps the section's length about the same.
Referee: uncertain. S6 describes how typesetting renders references with DOIs where available and how the evidence package pairs excerpts with records. The supplied text contains citation keys, and the rendered bibliography and evidence package are unavailable for inspection.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · fixed
Where does Galley’s claim-level verification fit relative to earlier scientific claim verification and citation-supported generation?
Asked: Credit these precedents and identify Galley’s proposed contribution in the action taken after a verification verdict.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), fixed: The search found no verified passage for the earlier definition of the scientific claim verification task, so the paper does not cite it. The precedents are credited through the verified sources instead. Claim–citation verification is credited to DeepSciVerify [@sadeghi2026deepsciverif]. Retrieval-supported citation in AI-written papers is credited to Oh et al. [@oh2026show]. The changed sentence says outright that verification predates galley and is not proposed as a contribution. It places galley's proposed contribution in the action taken on a claim after each verdict. The sentences that follow already set out that action: a claim may keep its scope, be narrowed, move to the next candidate citation, or become a hypothesis.
Referee: verified. S2 credits earlier claim–citation verification and retrieval-supported citation and identifies Galley's proposed contribution as the action it takes after each verdict.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
What establishes bibliographic provenance for works without a DOI?
Asked: Scope the provenance claim to the checks the manuscript documents and regenerate C35.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), limitation: S5 applies the verbatim check to every cited passage and the registry record only to works with a DOI. It now also states that the registry check does not cover cited works without a DOI (edit under F1-methods-8). C35 is regenerated by `reconcile`, which reads the final text against every ledger entry once review is done and narrows C35 to this wording. Referees read the ledger before that step, and S5 now states this as a limitation in 'Reconciling the ledger with the text' (edit under F1-methods-9). No edit to S5 can change C35 before then, so this answer adds no further edit.
Referee: disagrees. S5 scopes the two provenance checks correctly. The requested regeneration of C35 is still deferred to reconciliation.
Settled by Gemini 4 Carbon: adopt_author: The author's answer stands because Section 5 already scopes the provenance claim and review edits cannot modify Appendix A directly. The author and the referee agree that Section 5 applies the verbatim abstract check to every cited passage, limits the registry check to cited works with a DOI, and states that the registry check does not cover cited works without a DOI. The referee objects only that Appendix A still shows the unrevised wording of C35. Appendix A renders the claim ledger at typesetting and does not take direct text edits. On galley's behaviour ladder, the reconcile behaviour runs only after review finishes to align each ledger entry with the final text. Section 5 already states that revisions during review can leave the claim ledger inconsistent with the manuscript until the reconcile behaviour closes that gap.

citations referee, GPT-6.2 Sol · material · adjudicated
Which finding does each study support, and how does DeepSciVerify’s evidence scope compare with Galley’s?
Asked: Separate the attributions, describe DeepSciVerify’s evidence escalation, and regenerate C29 to match.
Author (Claude Opus 5.5), rebutted: The verdict confirms that S2 now does what the finding asks. Each study supports its own finding, and the text describes DeepSciVerify's escalation from abstract-level reasoning to passage-level evidence. The remaining objection is about C29, and C29 is an entry in the claim ledger, not text in S2. The edits in a response can only replace manuscript text, so no edit to S2 can change the ledger entry at this stage. The ledger is updated by the reconcile behavior after review ends. A family other than the author's reads the final text against every ledger claim and confirms it, narrows it to the text's wording or drops it. C29 will therefore be narrowed to the separate attributions and the escalation that S2 states. The ledger, evidence package and sign-off sheet then match the manuscript.
